title: You’ve probably heard Hagar’s name—but most people only know the surface of her story.
paragraphs: You’ve probably heard Hagar’s name—but most people only know the surface of her story.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Hagar’s story isn’t just about conflict.
It’s about being used, discarded… and still seen by God.
The Forgotten Woman in the Background
Hagar was an Egyptian servant in the household of Abraham and Sarah.

She wasn’t family.
She wasn’t chosen.
She didn’t have a voice.
And yet… she becomes central to one of the most emotionally raw moments in Scripture.
God had promised Abraham a son.

But time passed…
Waiting turned into doubt…
And doubt turned into human control.
So Sarah did something drastic—she gave Hagar to Abraham to bear a child (Genesis 16).

Hagar didn’t choose this.
She was used as a solution.
When Running Feels Like the Only Option
No plan. No provision. No future.
This is where most people think the story fades…
But this is where God steps in.
The God Who Sees the Unseen
In the desert, something extraordinary happens.
He speaks to her, gives her direction, and makes a promise about her son, Ishmael.
And Hagar responds with a name for God that changes everything:
“El Roi” — The God Who Sees Me

She was a servant.
A foreigner.
A woman with no status.
But Here’s the Part Most People Skip…
Years later, after Isaac is born, Hagar is cast out again.
Sent into the wilderness with almost nothing.
She places Ishmael under a bush and walks away, unable to watch him die.
And He calls out to Hagar.
He opens her eyes to a well of water that was already there.
The provision was present… but she couldn’t see it in her pain.
The Deeper Truth (This Is About You Too)
Because there are moments when you feel:

Used by others
Forgotten in the background
Cast out of places you thought were secure
Left in a wilderness you didn’t choose
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The same God who found Hagar in the wilderness is the God who sees you right now.
The Gospel Hidden in the Wilderness
Because one day, God would not just see suffering…

Where Hagar was cast out—
Jesus was rejected.

Where Hagar was rescued physically—
Jesus offers eternal rescue.
Because the real wilderness isn’t just physical.
And no amount of human effort can fix that.

To take your sin
To call you to repentance
To offer grace you cannot earn
To restore what was broken
Salvation is not about being “good enough.”
There’s a reason this story is pressing on your heart right now.
And this is just the surface.
But so is the God who meets you there.
